body:
Here are some tests:

| Changes | On OneDrive WebUI | On rclone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | foo‛＃bar.txt | foo＃bar.txt |
| None | foo＃baz.txt | foo#baz.txt |
| Remove `EncodeHash`* | foo‛＃bar.txt | foo‛‛＃bar.txt |
| Remove `EncodeHash`* | foo＃baz.txt | foo＃baz.txt (which is the same) |

\* means replacing `encoder.EncodeHashPercent` [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/master/fs/encodings/encodings.go#L190) to `encoder.EncodePercent`.
Just a quick thought but it looks #3723 may be related.

Onedrive filenames can't have `#` characters in them.  So to allow this rclone encodes them as `＃` (the full width unicode equivalent.

However if you do have files with `＃` in like you do then rclone will escape them with  `‛` so making `‛＃` as you've seen.

These files will round-trip back and forth with rclone properly, however will appear in the onedrive listing with the extra  `‛` 

So provided you use rclone to list/transfer files you'll never notice the extra  `‛` .

What problem is this causing you?

Maybe I should allow the escaping to be disabled - what do you think?

I think that OneDrive is now accepting `#` as part of the filename. I'm able to upload files with such filename and the filename of that file can be correctly displayed on Windows (at least non-UWP) client, Android client and WebUI.

From documentation and discussions on Microsoft, it seems that [# and % can be supported](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/microsoft-sharepoint-blog/new-support-for-and-in-sharepoint-online-and-onedrive-for/ba-p/60357) by Sharepoint administrators flipping a switch.

Another documentation listed [here](https://support.office.com/en-us/article/Invalid-file-names-and-file-types-in-OneDrive-OneDrive-for-Business-and-SharePoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa#invalidcharacters) also confirms that `#` and `%` are allowed for new versions of OneDrive. So maybe we can allow the escaping to be disabled, or even just remove the escaping altogether.
Thanks for looking that up!  So it looks like I need to make the encoding configurable - if I change it it will break the usage for existing users probably....

Please can you try this with the `--onedrive-encoding None` flag?  You can put that as `encoding = None` in your config.

That disables the character name conversion and should fix the problem for you.

https://beta.rclone.org/branch/v1.50.2-140-g222f1e7d-fix-encodings-beta/ (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

With the build you mentioned above (with `encoding = None` in my config), I can confirm that:
* Uploading/downloading file whose name contains "#" is working.
* Uploading/downloading file whose name contains "＃" is working.
* Uploading/downloading file whose name contains "＃" and "#" is working

In all cases, both of the symbols are intact.
I've merged this to master now which means it will be in [the latest beta](https://beta.rclone.org) in 15-30 mins and released in v1.51

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)
Arch Linux, 64 bit

####  Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)
OneDrive (for Business)

```
rclone sync /tmp/test one:/test
```
